title: Explicit bounds for primality testing and related problems
note: Exact statement, p. 372 (read in the AMS PDF): 'Theorem 2 (ERH). Let G be a nontrivial subgroup of Z/(m)* such that n ∈ G for all positive n < x. Then x < 2(log m)^2.' The PDF's OCR text layer drops the superscript and reads 'x < 2(log m) .'. The exponent 2 is confirmed by the abstract the AMS deposited with Crossref, which ends: 'if the ERH holds, a composite number m has a witness for its compositeness (in the sense of Miller or Solovay-Strassen) that is at most 2 log^2 m' (TeX '$2{\log^2}m$'). The zbMATH review also reads '2 log^2 m'. Here 'nontrivial' means proper (zbMATH review: 'a proper subgroup of (Z/mZ)^*'). The same page has 'Theorem 3 (ERH). Let G be a nontrivial subgroup of Z/(m)* such that n ∈ G for all positive n < x relatively prime to m. Then x < 3(log m)^2.' So the constant 2 counts all positive integers n < x, including those not prime to m; if the Lean target asks for a witness coprime to m, Bach's constant is 3. In Theorem 2, x < 2(log m)^2 means the least positive integer outside G is below 2(log m)^2 (zbMATH's review says 'must exceed', which is a slip). zbMATH links the JSTOR DOI 10.2307/2008811; the AMS DOI is given here.
cited_for: the explicit ERH bound 2(log m)^2 for the least integer outside a proper subgroup of (Z/mZ)^*
